newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi sees Japan firms' profit up 9.8% in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi sees Japan firms' profit up 9.8% in 96/97.

text.p: Parent current profits at Japan's leading companies are expected to rise by an average of 9.8 percent in 1996/97, Yamaichi Research Institute said in a report on Thursday.
It also said that the firms' parent current profits for the 1997/98 business year from April 1 are expected to grow by an average of 9.4 percent.
The report said the yen's retreat against the dollar, increased capital investment and a gradual recovery in consumption are expected to contribute to increased profits in the current year.
It also said that profits should continue to rise in the 1997/98 business year starting on April 1, mainly as a result of the weaker yen.

"Even though temporary repercussions from a two percentage point hike in the sales tax to five percent and the end of an extraordinary income tax break are inevitable, the yen's decline will be significantly positive," the report said.
It also predicted that the automobile industry will continue to lead Japanese industry through early 1998.
On a consolidated basis, the companies are expected to see group current profits grow by an average of 14.3 percent in 1996/97, and an average of 11.6 percent in 1997/98.
The report is based on a survey of 456 firms listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Yamaichi said.

Yamaichi Research also revised up its forecast for the average dollar-yen exchange rate in 1996/97 to 113 yen from a previous forecast of 110 yen three months ago. It also predicted that the exchange rate would average 120 yen in 1997/98, compared with its previous forecast of 110 yen.
Daiwa Research Institute said on Thursday that it expects parent current profits of Japan's leading firms to grow by an average of 9.7 percent in the year to March 31.
The research firm affiliated with Daiwa Securities Co Ltd said in a report that the expected rise in profits was mainly due to the yen's retreat against the dollar.
It said companies' parent current profits in 1997/98 would rise by an average of 12.0 percent thanks to the weaker yen and robust earnings in the automobile, electric appliance and steel industries.
Daiwa Research forecast an average dollar-yen rate of 113 yen in 1996/97 and 120 yen in 1997/98.
Its report was based on a survey of 547 firms listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's first section, excluding banks, brokerages and other financial institutions.
